madam president, european negotiators at the madrid climate talks like to position themselves as leaders on climate change, but we are still ignoring the science and failing to tell the truth on climate. the truth is that we need to achieve net zero carbon by 2030, and this means a radical transformation of the way we live across the european continent. we are also hypocrites, as we focus attention narrowly on our direct carbon emissions whilst ignoring the co2 embodied in the goods we consume that have been imported. the european green deal is pointless if we do not combine it with an enlightened trade policy. brazil’s president bolsonaro saw the provisional mercosur agreement as a green light to invite ranchers to destroy the amazon and murder its indigenous people. a genuine green deal means a radical shift towards low—energy lifestyles in our continent and an enlightened trade policy embedded in the protection of our precious climate, which we must respect as a common good for all humanity.
madam president, unfortunately the debate on trade agreements and trade in general is becoming increasingly ideologised and politicised. i have seen this in the last parliament, but it has got worse. recently, we've faced attempts to delay or even torpedo the consent process for a trade agreement with vietnam on the basis of fabricated accusations. now the mercosur agreement is on the table only because the european parliament's left does not like bolsonaro ruling brazil. instead of talking about tariffs, quotas, geographical indications, all the things that are related to trade policy, we are dealing here more and more with human rights, labour legislation, environmental standards. these are all topics that belong to other bodies of the european parliament than the committee on international trade. if we've imposed the green deal on ourselves, i respect that, but let's also respect that other countries in the world have chosen a different path. if we don't want to trade with them, we're going to get into a situation where we're going to slowly close our trade borders with almost everyone, and i don't think that's possible. so let's really bring the trade debate back to the business topics.
madam president, it is extraordinary that this parliament, this sitting, which this morning welcomed mr raoni and mr claudelice silva dos santos as finalists for the sakharov prize, defenders of the amazon rainforest, is this afternoon asking whether the eu-mercosur agreement is compatible with the green deal. no, it's not a good one. and we have to choose sides. we can either take the side of those who defend the amazon and the forest, or we can take the side of agribusiness. this question is merely a pretext to find excuses and to put us on the side of agribusiness. there is no possible match. this deal is a death sentence for the amazon. this deal is a prize for bolsonaro, yes, and when we say no to the deal we are also saying no to bolsonaro. this agreement is an insult to indigenous peoples, human rights defenders and defenders. this deal is throwing the paris agreement out the window, and if you have any questions, ask bolsonaro. he's already said he's withdrawing and i heard today that even without a deal, the paris agreement will remain. so i don't know, they're too gullible or they're too hypocritical and i'd rather be on the side of the defenders of the amazon than the hypocrites.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the trade relationship between mercosur and the european union today is worth, as is well known, more than 120 billion euros in goods and services. it is an important and valuable package which, as mr simon mentioned a moment ago, now lies within the commercial realm outside of specific rules that can preside over the expectations that many colleagues have mentioned, including, for example, expectations in relation to the green deal. well, it strikes me that the green party has decided to react so strongly to the fact that there is a popular president of the european commission who has made the green deal a priority. the reaction is disordered. they have decided, having been deprived of the subject that interests them most, to play the most dangerous game in politics, that of who gets the bigger shot to recover some space in that sphere which they normally managed. that's not how you do it. green deal is two words. green and deal, "deal" means agreement, sit down and think, it's a challenge for all of us or take responsibility for what you say. you want to block all trade deals? the proposal is that all trade deals, using the green deal's gag, must be blocked now, that is, do you want to turn the green deal not into a challenge for everyone, but into the grave of this continent? do you want to turn europe into a closed and unavailable continent? well, the green deal is a different story for us. we decided to work for the people, not for four votes like you are doing.
i'm not going to let you get away with this. you inherited a cuckoo egg. they have presented you with a document written in a completely foreign language which, as you can see from this debate, few of us understand because we cannot. today europe and the world speak a very different language, a very different set of values than they used to. this agreement, written over 20 years, glorifies a religion that no longer functions in the world today. a religion that puts money before human rights and climate protection, a religion that has led to the fact that today the amazon is burning and human rights are being violated in brazil. this hypocrisy cannot be supported by many of my colleagues in this house, and it is not supported by the people of our countries, the people who are taking to the streets to protest against these agreements. and that's why we have to do everything we can to make sure that this agreement is written in the language of the modern world, of people who are taking to the streets to defend human rights, to defend the climate. because how do we look at the people who, on the one hand, we give awards here for human rights in brazil or climate protection, and on the other hand, we sell these human rights and climate protection for more cars and more cell phones? this can't be happening.
madam president! ladies and gentlemen! we are faced with a serious dilemma today. on the one hand, the trade agreement with the mercosur countries is estimated to contribute eur 19 trillion to gdp. it is expected to generate €88 billion in trade in goods, €34 billion in services. on the other hand, we are aware that the agreement could contribute to the deforestation of perhaps the world's most valuable forest resource, the reservoir of biodiversity, the amazon forest, which is being cut down, burned down, mostly deliberately cleared to make room for crops, including forage. it is proposed that the trade agreement with the mercosur countries be used to enforce compliance by these countries with the provisions of the paris agreement and to halt deforestation in the amazon. however, it can also lead to an increase in co2 emissions caused by transport. will the mercosur agreement be able to enforce on our partners the level of reduction in the use of pesticides, plant protection products and fertilizers proposed by the new green deal, and thus meet the criteria of animal welfare and food safety that a french, german or polish farmer must meet? the eu-mercosur agreement is not the only form of pressure we have. we know, for example, that european banks are investing millions in south american agriculture that does not meet the equivalence criteria. so maybe it's worth taking a different approach. first the standards, then the agreement, as is the case with the accession of new candidate countries to the european union.

mr president, imagine a young boy, about 13 years old. he goes to school to get an education that every child deserves. imagine that the teacher, whom the boy trusts, lures the boy into a dark room and rapes him. the boy is very brave and speaks out about his story, but when he goes to a police station, he is raped again. the boy’s family is so ashamed that they threw him out of their house. but at least, they did not kill him. this is not an isolated incident. it is a reality for hundreds of confirmed cases in the afghani province of logar, where teachers and local authority officials have been implicated in the sexual abuse ring. and now, imagine that we would not do anything about it.
